title: Alignment via Training Against Probes Without Losing Monitorability
abstract: arXiv:2609.38645v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Models are usually aligned based on their observed outputs, using demonstrations, preference data, or reward signals. These objectives reward responses that look aligned. More capable models may learn to satisfy them without internalizing the intended behavior, for example by faking compliance during training. Such superficial compliance could be harder when the objective is defined on model internals rather than outputs. Therefore, we study probe-guided fine-tuning, using probes that detect undesired properties in model activations as a direct training signal. We evaluate linear and non-linear probes with different numbers of probes per layer across two alignment objectives: harmlessness and honesty. We find that training against probes that do not update during training is an easily exploitable objective, while continuously updated probes substantially reduce harmfulness and improve honesty while preserving utility. translated_title: 通过对抗探针训练实现对齐而不丧失可监控性
translated_abstract: 模型通常基于其观察到的输出进行对齐，使用示范数据、偏好数据或奖励信号。这些目标会奖励那些看起来对齐的响应。更强大的模型可能学会满足这些目标而不内化预期行为，例如在训练过程中伪装顺从。当目标定义在模型内部而非输出上时，这种表面顺从可能更难实现。因此，我们研究了探针引导的微调方法，使用检测模型激活中不良属性的探针作为直接训练信号。我们在两个对齐目标（无害性和诚实性）下评估了线性和非线性探针，以及每层不同数量的探针。我们发现，针对训练期间不更新的探针进行训练是一个容易被利用的目标，而持续更新的探针在保持效用的同时，能够显著减少有害性并提高诚实性。
tldr: 该研究提出探针引导微调方法，发现使用持续更新的探针作为直接训练信号能有效减少模型有害行为并提升诚实性，同时保持模型效用而不丧失可监控性，而静态探针则容易被模型利用规避。
